sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Companies Act (公司法), Articles 1, 128-130, 133-138, 156, 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 3, 6-8; Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by People of the Mainland Area (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法) applicable to PRC-origin shareholders; additional scrutiny under the Investment Commission review rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.) (經濟部商業司), with mandatory pre-approval by the Investment Commission (投資審議委員會) for foreign and Mainland-China investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Establishment Registration Application for a Company Limited by Shares (股份有限公司設立登記申請書), accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), subscriber minutes, director/supervisor consent forms, CPA capital verification report, and foreign investment approval letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed under the Taiwan Companies Act; however, the registered capital must be fully subscribed and actually paid in, certified by a R.O.C.-licensed CPA capital verification report (資本額查核報告書). The Investment Commission must approve the total investment amount before remittance; funds are remitted through a designated foreign exchange bank into the Company's capital account. No separate escrow account is statutorily required, but the bank remittance certificate serves as the escrow-equivalent proof for capital verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The issued ordinary shares are hereby subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholders; the paid-in capital shall be remitted to the Company's designated bank account and verified by a certified public accountant. (2) The registered office and statutory domicile is fixed at [Address], Taiwan, and the Chairman is authorized to file the relevant lease documents. (3) [●] is appointed Chairman and General Manager, and [●] is appointed Finance Supervisor, each authorised to sign incorporation filings, open bank accounts, engage counsel and auditors, and complete all registrations. (4) Execution may be delegated. (5) These resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Pre-Approval and Capital Remittance Authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.) (經濟部投資審議委員會)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online investment application through the Investment Commission's e-service portal. Provide a business plan covering the administration of the employee stock ownership trust (ISIC 6430), shareholder identity documents (including PRC-origin shareholder screening under the Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by People of the Mainland Area), and a capital introduction plan. Upon approval, obtain the Investment Approval Letter and remit the approved foreign currency through a designated domestic banking unit (DBU) within the approved period.
required_dossiers: Investment application form
Business and fund utilisation plan for ESOP trust administration
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Corporate certificates/passports of all JV shareholders, including PRC parent and Taiwan counter-party
Power of attorney for the local authorised representative
Negative-list compliance statement for PRC-origin investment
Financial statements or credit evidence of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Investment Commission's deficiency letter within 30 days; submit a revised investment plan and capital adequacy schedule; if the application is refused, file an administrative appeal (訴願) within 30 days of receipt of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Services, MOEA, Taiwan (R.O.C.) — online Company and Commerce Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name pre-application using the national company name database, selecting the exact corporate name with the suffix '股份有限公司' (Company Limited by Shares). Simultaneously reserve business scope codes corresponding to ISIC 6430 (trust administration). The name reservation is valid for one month with one renewal period.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation application form
Suggested Chinese and English name candidates
Business scope code list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-file with alternative names if the proposed name conflicts with an existing registration; file an opposition within 10 days against a conflicting superior name; request a business-scope reclassification if the portal assigns an incorrect code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription, Bank Account Opening, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated domestic banking unit (DBU) and R.O.C.-licensed Certified Public Accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital verification account in the proposed company name, receive the incoming foreign currency remittance, convert to New Taiwan Dollars, and obtain a bank deposit certificate. Retain a certified public accountant to review the remittance evidence and issue the CPA capital verification report (資本額查核報告書) confirming full subscription and payment of issued shares.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Foreign exchange remittance certificate (匯入匯款通知書)
Bank deposit certificate (存款證明)
Subscriber ledger and share subscription forms
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Identity cards/passports of directors and supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remittance amount or currency differs from the approved investment, arrange a supplementary remittance or return the excess funds through the same DBU and obtain a revised remittance certificate; instruct the CPA to re-issue the verification report after correcting the bank evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with the Company Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Services, MOEA, Taiwan (R.O.C.) — central registry; or the municipal commercial registration office where the registered office is located (e.g., Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment registration package online through the Company and Commerce Registration Portal. Attach the approved Articles of Incorporation, incorporation meeting minutes, director/supervisor appointment consents, CPA capital verification report, lease agreement with owner consent, building use clearance, and the Investment Commission approval letter. Pay the registration fee and collect the Certificate of Company Registration (公司登記證明書).
required_dossiers: Establishment registration application form
Articles of Incorporation (original with company chop)
Minutes of the incorporator and subscriber meeting
Director and supervisor appointment consents and resumes
CPA capital verification report
Lease agreement and landlord's consent letter
Building use permit or occupancy clearance
Investment Commission approval letter
Company name reservation certificate
Registration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure registry queries by filing supplementary documents within 30 days; if the registrar disputes the charter or capital structure, submit amended articles and re-file; after final refusal, file an administrative appeal before the Executive Yuan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Labour Insurance Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (regional office of the Ministry of Finance) and Bureau of Labour Insurance, Ministry of Labour; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete profit-seeking enterprise tax registration (營利事業所得稅登記), sales tax / uniform invoice registration (稅籍登記), and the integrated employer registration for Labour Insurance, Labour Pension, and National Health Insurance through the government single-portal linkage. Order the uniform invoice serial numbers for VAT issuance before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Tax registration application form (統一編號設立/變更登記)
Uniform invoice purchase application
Company chop and representative chop specimen cards
Employment records and payroll plan for initial officers
Labour insurance declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax filing window is missed, file a late tax registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau and pay any nominal penalty; for insurance registration errors, submit correction sheets to the Bureau of Labour Insurance within the monthly adjustment period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises Fire Safety, Occupational Safety, and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Fire Bureau (消防局) and Construction / Urban Development Bureau (建管處)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a self-inspection against the Fire Services Act; submit the application for fire safety equipment inspection (fire extinguishers, alarms, emergency lighting, and escape routes). Verify that the building occupancy permit authorises administrative office use (Group G-2); if the current certificate does not cover office use, apply for a change-of-use authorisation. Perform an occupational safety hazard assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for ergonomics, electrical safety, and first-aid readiness.
required_dossiers: Building use permit or occupancy certificate
Lease agreement
Fire safety equipment installation declaration and inspection checklist
Fire safety management statement (if 100+ employees)
Occupational safety self-inspection checklist
First-aid kit and emergency response plan confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify all fire-safety equipment deficiencies listed in the inspection report within the stated timeline; request a re-inspection after repairs. For building-use discrepancies, obtain a formal change-of-use certificate before the final occupancy approval. Apply for a temporary conditional clearance for non-life-safety corrections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the entity is an office-based employee stock ownership trust administrator (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 525920) and is not subject to any sectoral industrial licensing board; general commerce supervision is vested in the Department of Commercial Services, MOEA, Taiwan (R.O.C.). Should the JV later act as a professional third-party trustee holding out to the public, the Financial Supervisory Commission (金融監督管理委員會) would apply the Trust Enterprise Act licensing regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required under Taiwan law for administration of a captive employee stock ownership trust; a Trust Enterprise License (信託業執照) is optional and becomes mandatory only if the entity administers trusts for unaffiliated beneficiaries or solicits trust business from the public.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (R.O.C.) (環境部), formerly Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 5 — Exempt: office-based financial administration is not listed in the positive project schedules of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act Enforcement Rules; therefore no EIA report, abbreviated report, or registration certificate is required for this scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, combustion, or VOC emissions are generated. Any sanitary sewage (restrooms, canteen) must be discharged into the public sewer system or, if on-site treatment is used, must comply with Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards (pH 6-9; BOD5 ≤ 200 mg/L; SS ≤ 200 mg/L; COD ≤ 400 mg/L). General office and confidential-shredding waste must be handled under the Waste Management Act, with recycling of paper, plastics, and electronic equipment following Ministry of Environment recycling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: fire-protection equipment installation and annual inspection under Fire Services Act Articles 6, 10, and 13; maintain an emergency escape plan and, if more than 100 employees, establish a fire-safety management committee. Building: verify that the certificate of occupancy permits office use (Group G-2) and obtain any required change-of-use authorisation from the municipal Construction Bureau. Occupational: comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act — conduct ergonomics and electrical-safety hazard identification, provide first-aid equipment, register workplace risk assessments, and report any occupational accidents within the statutory 8-hour notification window.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, administered locally by the competent National Taxation Bureau; electronic tax services are provided through the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal and the integrated company-registration and business-registration systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sino-foreign equity joint venture must first complete entity establishment and business registration with the competent Taiwan company-registration authority, including foreign investment approval where applicable. The entity must then register its business-tax status with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable business activities. The tax authority issues or confirms the eight-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號), which functions as the entity's statutory tax and business identification number. Typical supporting documents include the approved articles of incorporation, company registration certificate, foreign investor approval documents, responsible-person identification, lease or premises evidence, business-scope description, bank-account information where requested, and an authorized-agent power of attorney. A foreign enterprise without a Taiwan company may require branch, representative-office, or other approved operating registration before obtaining a tax identity, depending on the activities performed. Changes to responsible persons, registered address, business scope, capital, or tax status must be reported within the applicable statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for companies. A Taiwan limited company or Sino-foreign equity joint venture is generally taxed as a separate legal person. Pass-through treatment is not available merely by election. Certain transparent or special regimes may arise from the legal form and governing trust, partnership, securities, or investment statutes, but an employee stock ownership trust must be analyzed separately from the operating joint venture. Taiwan generally has no broad hybrid-mismatch election that converts an ordinary company into a pass-through entity. Tax incentives, investment credits, and approved special regimes require satisfaction of their specific statutory conditions and do not change the entity's default legal tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Business Tax, principally a value-added tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The small-business exemption thresholds are generally NT$80,000 of monthly sales for goods and NT$40,000 of monthly sales for services. Businesses exceeding the applicable threshold, or otherwise carrying on taxable business requiring registration, must complete business-tax registration. The threshold does not eliminate registration or other tax obligations where a specific statutory registration requirement applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses an electronic-invoice platform and standardized electronic-invoice formats administered under Ministry of Finance rules. Covered business entities must issue, transmit, retain, and report electronic invoices in accordance with the applicable category-specific timetable and technical requirements. Electronic invoices are generally uploaded or transmitted through the Ministry of Finance platform or an approved electronic-invoice service provider; Taiwan does not operate a universal Latin American-style real-time pre-clearance model for every transaction. Business-to-business transactions, export transactions, allowance documents, cancellation documents, and financial or system-generated invoices may have different issuance and transmission requirements. Digital signatures, qualified certificates, authorized system access, invoice numbering, XML or prescribed-format data, audit trails, and retention controls may be required. The entity should verify current implementation dates and exemptions with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Taiwan may generally qualify for 0% business tax when the export is properly declared through customs and the taxpayer can establish that the goods physically left Taiwan. Qualifying export-related transactions may include goods sold for export, goods exported by the seller, and other transactions specifically recognized under the Business Tax Act and related regulations. Services may qualify for zero rating only where they fall within the statutory categories, such as services supplied to foreign customers and used outside Taiwan or other expressly recognized cross-border services. The taxpayer must establish the customer, contractual scope, place and use of the service, consideration, payment trail, and documentary evidence supporting offshore use. Zero rating does not automatically apply merely because the customer is non-Taiwanese or payment is received in foreign currency. Input business tax refunds require valid tax invoices or approved documents, reconciliation to books and tax returns, and satisfaction of the statutory refund conditions. Unsupported, incorrectly classified, or subsequently cancelled exports may be reassessed at the applicable business-tax rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs export declaration or electronically filed export declaration bearing the relevant customs acceptance or release information
Commercial invoice and packing list, where applicable
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other transport document evidencing shipment from Taiwan
Sales contract, purchase order, or equivalent export transaction record
Proof of export, customs release, or other evidence that the goods physically departed Taiwan
Electronic invoice or other legally prescribed sales document, with zero-rate coding where required
For offshore services: service agreement, customer and beneficiary evidence, deliverables, timesheets or service records where relevant, and evidence that the service was used outside Taiwan

Bank remittance advice, inward-remittance record, or other payment evidence where required to substantiate consideration; this is not a universal substitute for customs export evidence and is not independently sufficient for every zero-rated transaction
Import or export permits, certificates of origin, inspection records, or sector-specific approvals where required by the goods or transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan does not impose a universal 180-day foreign-exchange-repatriation rule that independently determines business-tax zero-rating for every export transaction. The 180-day value should therefore be treated as a compliance-control parameter requiring confirmation against the transaction type, banking rules, contract terms, and current Central Bank requirements. Failure to collect or document export proceeds may trigger banking, foreign-exchange, customs, or tax review, but does not automatically establish taxable treatment without analysis of the underlying transaction. During a tax audit, the National Taxation Bureau may require customs records, transport evidence, contracts, invoices, payment records, service-use evidence, and reconciliation to accounting books and VAT returns. If zero-rating is denied, the authority may assess the applicable 5% business tax, interest, late-payment charges, and statutory penalties; input-tax refunds may be clawed back and previously refunded amounts recovered. False invoices, fabricated export records, concealment of taxable sales, or intentional tax evasion may additionally result in administrative fines, suspension or cancellation of invoice privileges, customs consequences, and criminal liability under applicable Taiwan tax and criminal laws. Voluntary correction before audit, prompt repayment, complete records, and documented internal controls may reduce exposure but do not eliminate statutory liabilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (中国人民银行, PBoC) as the central bank, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (国家外汇管理局, SAFE) exercising delegated FX administration under State Council authorization. Cross-strait capital flows involving the Taiwan jurisdiction are additionally governed by the Law on the Protection of Investment by Taiwanese Compatriots (台湾同胞投资保护法) and the 2015 Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation and Strengthening of Tax Cooperation Agreement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CNY is freely convertible on the current account (goods, services, dividends, interest) since China's IMF Article VIII commitment, subject to bank-conducted authenticity and legality review under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (国务院令第532号, as amended) and the SAFE Trade in Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Capital account items (FDI equity injection, cross-border ESOP sponsor loans, equity transfers of trust-held shares, external debt) remain registration-based: FDI capital must obtain SAFE registration before receipt, be credited to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account (外汇资本金账户), and may only be settled under the proceeds-commitment / voluntary settlement regime (支付命令函, 意愿结汇 per 汇发〔2016〕16号). Dividend and profit remittance by the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is classified as current account and requires the Outward Payment Tax Filing Certificate (对外支付税务备案表), audited financial statements, and a board profit-distribution resolution; the Taiwanese shareholder's dividend benefits from a treaty-reduced 5% withholding if its direct shareholding is 25% or more and substance conditions are met, otherwise the domestic 10% withholding applies. TWD (新台币) is not a freely convertible listed currency on the China interbank market; Taiwan-side capital injection is therefore typically denominated in USD or CNY, with TWD conversion executed via USD on the offshore leg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory export-proceeds surrender and fixed statutory conversion ratios were abolished by SAFE Announcement No.1 of 2012. Export receipts must still be repatriated into mainland China and monitored through the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System (货物贸易外汇监测系统); A-class enterprises may settle at the bank counter without case-by-case SAFE approval, while B/C-class enterprises face documentary examination for each transaction. Amounts outstanding beyond the contractually agreed collection period (customs practice 90 days per the Single Window norm) combined with abnormal overdue-collection ratios can trigger a downgrade from A to B/C classification. There is no statutory minimum percentage of export proceeds that must be converted into CNY; the JV may retain foreign currency in its current-account FX account or settle at will. ESOP-related cross-border sale proceeds are capital-account receipts and require separate SAFE registration under employee equity incentive FX rules (汇发〔2012〕7号), not the trade-monitoring surrender regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; no routine filing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may incur administrative fines and liability for failure to convene or present accounts; Taiwan has no automatic annual-return strike-off timetable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 1 May to 31 May following the calendar tax year; extensions may apply for approved non-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty generally applies, together with tax assessment and interest; failure to file may result in tax authority assessment based on available information and additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements, where statutory audit criteria are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; submission to a government authority is generally not required solely because an audit is performed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completion before submission of financial statements to the annual shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain required CPA certification or present compliant accounts may trigger director liability, administrative fines, tax adjustments, and restrictions on statutory approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership and controlling-person review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; Ministry of Economic Affairs and competent AML authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general Taiwan annual UBO filing; review annually and update promptly after any ownership, control, director, or registered-information change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or provide required ownership information may result in AML-related administrative penalties, enhanced scrutiny, and restrictions by financial institutions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review of company registration particulars and share register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal records; Ministry of Economic Affairs for reportable amendments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Conduct annually; report changes generally within 15 days after the change, subject to the applicable filing rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted amendment registration may result in administrative fines and continuing penalties; no general annual franchise renewal fee applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit and certification are generally required for companies with paid-in capital of at least NT$30 million, public companies, financial institutions, and entities covered by sector-specific rules. Additional tax-audit requirements may apply under Taiwan tax regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards, substantially converged with IFRS. Public companies and specified entities follow applicable IFRS-based requirements; other companies generally apply Taiwan GAAP and the Business Accounting Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan generally does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. The company must maintain current ownership and controlling-person information, record share transfers in the share register, and update reportable corporate information promptly. Any PRC-related ownership or investment-control restrictions require separate review.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,500 annually for a Taiwan registered office or corporate secretarial service; a registered agent is not generally mandatory as a separate legal role.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-12,000 for a non-public company, depending on capital, transaction volume, foreign-investment complexity, and whether tax certification is also required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to an ESOP administration joint venture. The standard 20% CIT rate applies to all taxable income. Retained earnings not distributed within the statutory time frame attract an additional 5% retained-earnings surtax under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act. Qualified research and development or investment incentive credits may reduce the effective rate only if the JV conducts qualifying R&D in Taiwan, which is atypical for an ESOP trust administrator.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (Chinese: 營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing and Payment Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year fiscal year, file between May 1 and May 31 of the following year. For a fiscal year ending on a non-calendar date, file within five months after the close of the fiscal year. Where the annual financial statements are audited and signed by a certified public accountant, the deadline for calendar-year filers is extended to June 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: unified business number, legal name, registered address, industrial code, and fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-invested JV must provide its Taiwan tax registration and local contact officer; attach a Chinese-language power of attorney if the responsible person is outside Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and sales: all service fees, commissions, and administrative charges for ESOP trust administration, payroll wiring, share valuation, and equity transfer facilitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare Taiwan-sourced gross receipts in full. Fees recharged to the offshore parent under a cost-contribution or service agreement must be supported by actual invoices and evidence that the JV bore the corresponding functions, assets, and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs and expenses: direct salaries for ESOP administrators, IT infrastructure, office lease, market data subscriptions, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate actual expenses incurred in Taiwan. Payments to the non-resident parent for management services, software, or platform access must satisfy arm’s-length substance requirements; otherwise the expenses may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and gains: interest on in-house cash pools, foreign exchange gains, gains from disposal of treasury shares, and any passive income received by the trust administration JV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Taiwan-source interest, dividends, and equity-linked gains. Any withholding tax already deducted by the payor may be claimed as a credit if the relevant Form 551 certificate is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: prior-year net operating losses (NOL), tax credits, and previously unreported reversal of tax reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NOL claims require complete audited books and records and are limited to the 10-year carryforward. Offshore parent losses cannot be transferred into the Taiwan JV unless a valid branch/PE consolidation exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic tax calculation: taxable income multiplied by 20% statutory CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the flat 20% rate. Do not adjust for a tax treaty with Mainland China because no effective cross-strait DTA is accepted for withholding or return purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Minimum tax and excessive tax preference items (Alternative Minimum Tax under Article 42, Income Basic Amount Act).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the JV enjoys any tax preference that reduces its regular tax below the 12% AMT threshold, complete the AMT schedule. ESOP trusts normally have no applicable preferences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure schedule: intercompany service fees, management charges, loans, royalties, share transfers, and dividend distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fully disclose all controlled transactions with the Chinese parent; attach the transfer pricing report if the NT$100 million documentary threshold is met; failure to disclose can trigger penalty assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 2% of the assessed tax for each partial or complete month of delay, capped at 20% of the tax due (Income Tax Act Art. 108). A return filed with deliberate understatement or omission is subject to a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax (Art. 110). Administrative interest at the statutory benchmark rate accrues from the original filing deadline until full payment. In egregious cases, the tax authority may notify the company to file and impose an additional assessment plus criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders (including Mainland Chinese corporate/individual investors), effective from the 2018 tax reform. Prior years were 20%. The rate is final and is levied on the gross dividend. No reduced domestic rate applies to a Mainland China investor because no cross-strait DTA is in force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For jurisdictions with an effective Taiwan tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must submit a Certificate of Residence (tax residency certificate) and a completed treaty rate application to the Taiwan paying company prior to the dividend distribution. The payer then withholds at the reduced treaty rate if approved; alternatively, the excess tax may be reclaimed by filing a refund application with the National Taxation Bureau within ten years. With respect to Mainland China, the cross-strait tax arrangement is not applied as a full DTA, and the 21% statutory withholding rate must be implemented; any de facto relief requires a case-level ruling from the Ministry of Finance, which is rare.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic statutory withholding is 20% of gross payments to non-resident enterprises; most Taiwan DTAs provide a 10% rate for royalties. Interest: domestic statutory withholding is 15% for most non-resident corporate interest recipients (20% for certain non-financial offshore lenders); treaty rates commonly range from 0–10% if a DTA applies. For Mainland China, no treaty relief is available; royalties are withheld at 20% and interest at 15% (or 20% if the lender is not a qualified financial institution).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory local file/master file preparation and TP report are triggered when the aggregate annual related-party transaction amount exceeds NT$100 million (approximately USD 3.3 million). An SME exemption may apply to enterprises with related-party transactions below NT$100 million and total revenue below NT$100 million, but the disclosure schedule must still be attached. Country-by-country reporting applies to MNE groups with parent-group consolidated revenue exceeding NT$10 billion (approximately USD 330 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not have a general Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) statute akin to the UAE, but the Income Tax Act Articles 12-1 and 12-3 embody a broad general anti-avoidance rule and judicial substance-over-form principles. For an ESOP trust administration JV, the enterprise must demonstrate real business substance in Taiwan: physical office, full-time administrative and compliance personnel, board minutes, independent accounts, and documented decision-making functions. A JV operating as a shell with no Taiwan employees or office, or merely channelling dividends derived from mainland-linked treasury shares, will be recharacterized, deductions denied, profits allocated to the beneficial parent, and potentially the investment approval revoked.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or understating service fees received from the mainland parent or its affiliates for ESOP administration, payroll wiring, and share transfer facilitation; recording parent recharges as shareholders’ equity or loans rather than taxable revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, a penalty is imposed on the amount of underpaid tax, ranging from 0.5 to three times the understated tax. Criminal tax evasion under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act carries imprisonment for up to five years and/or a criminal fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director and finance officer are jointly and severally liable for unpaid company taxes if they caused or allowed asset concealment (Tax Collection Act Art. 6). The National Taxation Bureau may apply to the court for a travel ban, and the director’s personal assets may be attached to satisfy the tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or maintaining the Taiwan JV solely as a conduit to receive mainland-controlled ESOP dividends or share-purchase benefits without a physical Taiwan office, employees, operational records, or independent board; nominee shareholder arrangements to circumvent investment approval requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Investment Commission (MOEA) may revoke the mainland investment approval under the Statute for Investment by Mainland China and order divestment. The National Taxation Bureau may disregard the JV’s legal personality, allocate its income to the Real Beneficial Owner, and assess tax at 21% withholding plus 20% CIT with a penalty of up to three times the deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and nominal shareholders may be ordered to return all distributed funds to the company (Company Law Art. 23). Civil restitution claims, administrative debarment from serving as directors, and incapability to hold a passport may be imposed; criminal banking or securities charges can result in imprisonment if the structure qualifies as a financial fraud or false disclosure offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering via ESOP Trust
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ESOP trust administration JV as a conduit for unexplained cross-border remittances: accepting funds from the mainland parent without matching equity or distribution entitlements, executing wire transfers on behalf of undisclosed ultimate beneficiaries, failing to perform customer due diligence, or failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) for unusual share transfer payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Money Laundering Control Act (as amended in 2018) imposes administrative fines of NT$1 million to NT$10 million on trust service companies and their directors for non-compliance with internal control and reporting obligations (Art. 18). If the activity is willful, the responsible person is subject to imprisonment of six months to five years, and the JV is subject to corporate criminal fines (Art. 20).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, trustees, and AML compliance officers can be prosecuted individually and face disgorgement of all fees plus personal monetary fines. The court may order freezing of bank accounts, seizure of assets, and prohibition on leaving Taiwan; the JV license or business scope certificate may be cancelled by the competent authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arranging service fees, management charges, software royalties, or interest payments to the mainland parent so as to shift taxable profits outside Taiwan; using fabricated cost allocations or excessive debt interest without an arm’s-length benchmark study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will adjust the taxable income to the arm’s-length result under the Taiwan Transfer Pricing Regulations. The adjusted tax is assessed at 20% with interest; a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax applies under Income Tax Act Article 110. Failure to prepare the mandatory TP report within the statutory period also triggers a separate penalty of NT$50,000 to NT$100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or cause false TP documentation may bear civil liability for resulting tax penalties and may be referred to the tax prosecutor for criminal fraud. If the TP file is deemed fraudulent, the officer can be sentenced to imprisonment for up to five years and be personally responsible for restitution of the tax loss.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Distribution / Capital Maintenance Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to the mainland shareholder out of capital reserves or without sufficient accumulated earnings, or distributing profits while the JV is insolvent, thereby eroding the statutory capital without court approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Company Law, distributions of dividends must be made only from the company’s annual surplus. Directors are liable to restore the full amount of unlawful distributions; administrative fines of NT$100,000 to NT$2 million may be imposed by the competent authority (Company Law Art. 89).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director and supervisor who approved or executed the distribution bears personal and joint liability to creditors and shareholders for the amount illegally distributed. Bankruptcy proceedings and disqualification from business management may result; in severe cases with intent to defraud creditors, criminal liability under Company Law Article 23 and the Criminal Code (fraud) applies, carrying imprisonment.
